_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Guinea-Bissau covering Kaabu Empire, Portuguese Guinea, Amílcar Cabral's PAIGC liberation war, coups, and narco-state dynamics.

ethnic_groups.name: Balanta
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest group; southern Guinea-Bissau; rice farmers; stateless society tradition; majority animist; dominated PAIGC liberation army

ethnic_groups.name: Fula/Fulani (Fula/Fulbe)
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern and eastern regions; Gabú; Fouta Djallon links; predominantly Muslim; pastoralist heritage; commercial and political influence

ethnic_groups.name: Manjaco (Manjak)
ethnic_groups.notes: Northwestern coastal; Cacheu region; rice cultivation; cross-border with Senegal (Casamance)

ethnic_groups.name: Mandinka (Mandinga)
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern Guinea-Bissau; Gabú region; remnants of Kaabu Empire; Muslim; Mande people; strong Mali Empire heritage

ethnic_groups.name: Papel (Pepel)
ethnic_groups.notes: Bissau and Biombo region; coastal agriculturalists; rice growers

ethnic_groups.name: Bijagó (Bissagos Islanders)
ethnic_groups.notes: Bijagós Archipelago; distinct maritime culture; matrilineal; historically resisted Portuguese until 20th century

ethnic_groups.name: Mancanha
ethnic_groups.notes: Central coastal; related to Papel and Manjaco

ethnic_groups.name: Beafada
ethnic_groups.notes: Central Guinea-Bissau; related to Tenda group

ethnic_groups.name: Felupe/Jola
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern border; rice farmers; Casamance cultural area

ethnic_groups.name: Nalu
ethnic_groups.notes: Northwestern coastal; related to Guinea groups

ethnic_groups.name: Other (including Cape Verdean, Lebanese, Portuguese)
ethnic_groups.notes: Cape Verdean Creoles influential; Lebanese traders; small Portuguese community

natural_resources.notes: Cashew nuts dominant export (6th globally, 85% of export earnings); fishing (rich waters, EU fishing agreements); Bijagós Archipelago UNESCO Biosphere Reserve; offshore oil potential (disputed with Senegal, now joint development); timber; largely agrarian economy

military.notes: Chronically unstable military—4 successful coups since independence (1980, 1999, 2003, 2012); military-narco nexus (cocaine transit from Latin America to Europe, 'Africa's first narco-state'); ECOWAS ECOMIB stabilization force; February 2022 coup attempt failed

infrastructure.notes: Very poor infrastructure; MTN and Orange operate; most roads unpaved.

debt_aid.notes: Heavily aid-dependent; HIPC debt relief; cashew monoculture vulnerability; narco-economy (cocaine transit estimated worth more than GDP); political instability deters investment

education.notes: Portuguese-language instruction; Kriol (creole) spoken widely; very low educational attainment; Amílcar Cabral's education legacy (revolutionary schools in liberated zones); Catholic mission schools significant; gender gap severe

diaspora_migration.notes: Portuguese connection primary migration route; Lusophone diaspora networks; Bijagós islanders relatively isolated; narcotics-related migration patterns; seasonal workers in Senegal/Gambia

digital_economy.notes: Minimal digital infrastructure; Orange Bissau primary telecom; among lowest internet penetration in Africa; no meaningful tech ecosystem; power supply unreliable; AfricaConnect improving backbone

country_profile.notes_unique: Bijagos Archipelago is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve; the country has experienced multiple coups; cashew nuts are the primary export (~90% of export earnings).
country_profile.national_anthem: Esta É a Nossa Pátria Bem Amada (This Is Our Beloved Homeland)

geography.terrain: Mostly low-lying; coastal marshes and mangroves; flat interior with some forested hills
geography.notes: Bijagós Archipelago (88 islands, UNESCO Biosphere Reserve); one of first Lusophone African independence countries (1973); extensive mangrove systems.

economy_extended.notes: Cashew nut dependent (~80% exports, top 5 global producer); narco-state label (cocaine transit from Latin America); extremely fragile state.

health.notes: One of highest maternal mortality rates globally; Raoul Follereau Hospital (Bissau) major facility; NGOs provide significant health services.

food_agriculture.notes: Cashew nuts dominant export; rice staple but deficit; mangrove rice cultivation traditional.

energy.notes: One of lowest electricity access rates globally; diesel generators dominate; solar projects emerging; OMVG dam project planned.

transport.notes: Very limited infrastructure; most roads unpaved; boat transport to Bijagós islands.

tourism.notes: Bijagós Archipelago UNESCO Biosphere; saltwater hippos unique attraction; largely undeveloped tourism; Portuguese heritage.

human_rights_gender.notes: Chronic political instability (4 coups since 1980); drug trafficking influence; FGM practiced despite ban; one of few African countries where homosexuality is legal.

security_stability.notes: Feb 2022 attempted coup; narco-trafficking transit hub; ECOWAS stabilization force; political instability chronic.

cultural_heritage.media_landscape: Fragile; Radio Bombolom; state RDN; private media limited
cultural_heritage.notes: Amílcar Cabral one of Africa's greatest independence thinkers; gumbe music unique; Carnival celebrated widely; Bijagós matrilineal society.

legal_system.customary_law_role: Significant in rural areas; tabanka councils
legal_system.notes: UEMOA/OHADA business law harmonization; political instability undermines rule of law; ineffective judiciary.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: One of world's most fragile states.
